items.english: Outside the door, dark by now, was the sound of hard rain and wind. It is a storm.

The parents and the child had gathered at the table under the dim electric light hanging against the wall of the narrow room, about to have their supper. Father and mother were both still truly young. And the child was a round and fat little girl, just able to stand holding on to the table.

Neither the man nor the woman had a single wrinkle yet in the face. But in the man's hollowed, kind-looking eyes in the shadow of his thick eyebrows there showed a drowsy colour of weariness. And in the woman's dark hair and about her slender shoulders there showed a still more sunken deep weariness, and a drowsy peace.
One day had ended. That day's sorrow and suffering were about to flow away into the peace of the night. And they, smiling in silence, fixed their eyes upon everything of that child.

The child, standing unsteadily, with fat and round arms short as balls, tried to sweep at everything on the table, without a moment's pause and far too fast. So, smiling, they set all the bowls and the teapot and the aluminum pot under the table. Left on the table were only the small spoon the child held and a single small plate.
But the child gave a noisy cry full of small joy and banged the spoon and the plate down on the table.

data.say: Drafted the opening storm and table scene in spare present-past English.
